# Windows Computer Use & Browser FastMCP Server
> Enterprise-grade Model Context Protocol (MCP) server providing deep Windows desktop operating system control, occlusion-proof DWM GPU window capture, 40ms Start Menu app resolver, and fast Playwright browser suite.

## Core Concepts & Documentation
- [Architecture & Overview](https://github.com/k39139215-gif/win-computer-mcp#readme): Complete system architecture, safety guardrails, and tool catalog.
- [DWM Window Capture](https://github.com/k39139215-gif/win-computer-mcp#-key-capabilities): Occlusion-proof GPU buffer rendering eliminating black box artifacts.
- [Start Menu App Resolver](https://github.com/k39139215-gif/win-computer-mcp#-key-capabilities): Sub-40ms fuzzy matching and execution of installed Windows desktop and UWP applications.
- [Playwright Browser Suite](https://github.com/k39139215-gif/win-computer-mcp#-key-capabilities): Multi-action batch execution (`browser_batch`) in <100ms.
- [Safety & Guardrails](https://github.com/k39139215-gif/win-computer-mcp): Command blocklists, rate limiting, and audit logging.

## Installation & Cursor AI Configuration
```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "win-computer-mcp": {
      "command": "python",
      "args": ["server.py"]
    }
  }
}
```

## Available MCP Tools
- `screenshot(window_title, monitor_index)`: High-fidelity screen or window capture using DWM GPU buffer.
- `launch_app(app_name, args)`: Fast 40ms Start Menu fuzzy-resolved app launcher.
- `list_windows()`: Instant Win32 window z-order and state enumeration (<2ms).
- `focus_window(title)`: Native foreground window activation and input focus.
- `browser_batch(actions)`: Multi-action browser pipeline in a single synchronous call (<100ms).
- `browser_snapshot()`: 15ms DOM snapshot of visible interactive elements with CSS selectors.
- `browser_eval(script)`: In-page JavaScript evaluation in <3ms.
- `mouse_click(x, y, button, double)`: Precision cursor dispatch.
- `type_text(text)`: Native keyboard simulation.
- `hotkey(keys)`: Dispatches complex Windows shortcuts (e.g., `["ctrl", "shift", "esc"]`).
